title: Come unto Me, When Shadows Darkly Gather
description: Come unto Me, When Shadows Darkly Gather in Tonic Solfa to WESLEY (MASON), doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 160, “"Come unto Me."”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WESLEY (MASON); any other Elevens and Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come un-to me, when sha-dows dark-ly ga-ther, When the sad heart is wea-ry and dis-trest, Seek-ing for com-fort from your Heav-enly Fa-ther, Come un-to me, and I will give you rest!

lines: Come unto me, when shadows darkly gather,
When the sad heart is weary and distrest,
Seeking for comfort from your Heavenly Father,
Come unto me, and I will give you rest!
Ye who have mourned when the spring-flowers were taken,
When the ripe fruit fell richly to the ground,
When the loved slept, in brighter homes to waken,
Where their pale brows with spirit-wreaths are crowned;
Large are the mansions in thy Father's dwelling,
Glad are the homes that sorrows never dim;
Sweet are the harps in holy music swelling,
Soft are the tones which raise the heavenly hymn;
There, like an Eden blossoming in gladness,
Bloom the fair flowers the earth too rudely pressed;
Come unto me, all ye who droop in sadness,
Come unto me, and I will give you rest.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to WESLEY (MASON) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
